reason: A concrete counterexample, rather than the asserted universal implication, refutes exactly the canonical printed pairwise-independence rule. The normalized real XOR law has positive treatment/control marginals; every fitting input is individually independent of the focal treatment; fixed potential outcomes (1,0) make the observed inputs precisely the two nonfocal bits; the deterministic polynomial fit uses only those inputs and equals the focal indicator, with covariance 1/4. The canonical rule explicitly permits any deterministic function of any or all such individually independent outcomes, so joint-vector independence is not an omitted condition. The single-input footnote and the valid independent-assignment/block examples need not be refuted.

A negation of a necessary sub-conjunction of the canonical numerical assertions is a valid refutation of the claim that all those assertions hold. The theorem also asserts all FE denominators positive and unique finite logistic fits. All 16 unit records, the 90 equally likely independent within-block allocations, FE-with-covariate residualization, opposite-block OLS residuals, opposite-block logistic likelihood/predictions, N=16 cluster-total HT, and equation [35] variance estimator agree with the printed specifications. The blind observation that prediction reverses the likelihood stratum selector is intentional opposite-block fitting, as required by Section 7.1, p.148. Already the exact FE mean, approximately -0.01398742627, does not round to -0.012. Negating the conjunction does not claim to refute every listed entry or the unformalized RE column.

All observed/potential masking equalities for the two HT totals, both unbiased-total assertions, and ATE unbiasedness are present. UnitExperiment ranges over every nonnegative normalized real law on the complete finite binary assignment space with both marginals strictly positive for each unit, with arbitrary fixed real potential outcomes and the actual nonzero population cardinal. No independence, fixed allocation count, or equal marginal hypothesis is added.

The actual target is T21WholeStatement. Its first conjunct gives all supportwise unit-count and actual-difference-in-means identities and unbiasedness under the exact conditions of (a). Its second gives the original-unit equation [12] contrast and unbiasedness for every nonempty partition with the canonical equal cluster marginals, including distinct cluster indicators from the standing assumptions, without imposing a fixed realized cluster count beyond canonical formal clause (b). Its third is a real four-unit experiment satisfying (b), positive treated and control counts on support, and actual difference-in-means bias 1/9 with ATE and expected HT zero, establishing (c). No zero denominator affects supported means or expectations.

For every finite binary assignment law with positive marginals and arbitrary real assignment-dependent common prediction, zero treatment-indicator/prediction covariance at every unit implies both generalized-total expectation identities and ATE unbiasedness. The fixed-prediction subcase explicitly includes zero covariances and all three expectations. The equation [16] identity is assignmentwise and outside the covariance antecedent. UnitExperiment encodes precisely the standing design law; the same prediction is used for both arms as in [13]-[16]. All denominators are positive and all moments are finite.
